details:
Q1: What should this issue deliver, given the root cause is unknown?
Choices:
A) Reproduce first: run `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` on the PR #6922 head (`481d3df`). Fix the code only if a test fails there. If nothing fails, make no code change and close the issue as a transient or cancellation side effect. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Better diagnostics only: extend the shard summary loop in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (lines 1417-1442) so each failed shard's `::error::` line also names its failing test(s) and first error line. Future log tails will then show the cause. Make no poller code change.
C) Both A and B: try to reproduce and fix, and also add the per-shard failing-test names to the `::error::` annotation.
D) Wait for a human to paste the failing shard's `FAIL` lines from run 37920705068 into this issue before planning.
**Note:** B and C edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. That needs `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=true` and an exact `files_touched` grant under the automation-path guard.
Q2: Which branch should a fix target?
Choices:
A) PR #6922's head branch `ai/issue-6908`, since the failure was seen on that PR's head and may come from its diff. (RECOMMENDED)
B) The default branch `main`, treating it as a defect already on main.
C) `main` for a diagnostics-only change (Q1 B), and `ai/issue-6908` for any test or poller fix.
**Note:** with Q1 D, the target follows whatever the pasted failure shows.
Q3: Should this issue also look at why `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` was cancelled?
Choices:
A) No. Leave that job's cancellation out of scope; it may simply follow the run being cancelled or superseded, and a separate triage can handle it if it happens again. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Yes, but investigate only. Report whether it hit its 20-minute `timeout-minutes` and make no timeout change.
C) Yes, and raise that job's timeout if the investigation shows it hit the 20-minute limit.
